extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists, editors and newsroom staff (reporters, photographers, video journalists, desk editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and operational standards and style guidance for producing, attributing, editing and publishing news across Reuters text, photos and video, including ethics, sourcing, corrections, independence and handling of risky material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always hold accuracy sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is paramount; getting it right takes precedence over speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy, as well as balance, always takes precedence over speed. Consider how you would withstand a challenge or denial before pushing the button. It is better to be late than wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always correct an error openly
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectify errors promptly and clearly in stories, captions, graphics or scripts; do not disguise or bury corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections must be transparent and promptly made. Do not hide corrections in subsequent leads or stories. Follow the detailed Corrections Policy in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always strive for balance and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Report fairly and impartially, reflecting all relevant sides without adopting one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask 'What do I know?' and 'What do I need to know?' Give subjects an opportunity to put their side, weigh space appropriately (victims may warrant more space than perpetrators), and avoid word choices that imply judgment or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always reveal a conflict of interest to a manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any personal circumstance that could give rise to a suspicion of bias or conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you think there is potential for conflict (financial, personal, outside work, etc.) raise it with your manager for guidance and possible recusal or mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always respect privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat privileged or confidential information appropriately and protect legally sensitive material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve confidential sources and privileged material unless required to disclose on legitimate editorial grounds to a supervisor; follow guidance on protected information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always protect their sources from the authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguard confidentiality of sources, including resisting inappropriate disclosure to authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source confidentiality is paramount. A source's compact is with Reuters; protect reporters' sources and supervisors must safeguard confidentiality. Disclose to a supervisor only on legitimate editorial grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always guard against putting their opinion in a news story
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not insert journalists' personal opinions into factual news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinions must be confined to clearly labelled opinion pieces; news stories, voiced video, scripts and work-related blogs should avoid reporter opinion. If analysis is provided, it must rely on facts and named sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never fabricate or plagiarise
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid all fabrication and plagiarism; it is a cardinal sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication and plagiarism are grounds for disciplinary action up to dismissal. Always attribute and verify; do not invent facts or copy without attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never alter a still or moving image beyond the requirements of normal image enhancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not manipulate images or video in ways that change reality beyond standard enhancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image alterations that add to or detract from reality may constitute fabrication. Follow Photos and Video sections for permitted enhancement; major changes require senior-editor approval and may lead to dismissal if improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never pay for a story and never accept a bribe
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not offer or accept payments or other improper inducements to obtain news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments or gifts to influence sources are forbidden. Limited narrow exceptions (risk to life, facilitating administrative processes) require manager approval, accurate expense reporting and escalation to legal counsel where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy for how errors are handled: open, prompt, and not hidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectify errors promptly and clearly in stories, captions, graphics or scripts. Do not disguise or bury corrections in later material. Follow the Handbook's Corrections Policy for procedures and wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use named sources where possible; be honest and transparent about sources and seek corroboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer Reuters journalists/cameras on the spot; use named sources rather than anonymous when possible. Anonymous sources are weakest; use them only in exceptional cases for information of market or public interest and subject to authorization. Take notes, record interviews, cross-check information, weigh unnamed sources' track records and motives, and talk to sources on all sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes are sacrosanct and must not be altered other than trivial deletions that do not change sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter quotes except to remove redundant words without changing meaning. When translating, ensure idiomatic equivalence and preserve tone. Use paraphrase when appropriate; consult senior editor if dilemma about running an awkward or damaging verbatim quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflecting reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories and images must reflect reality; avoid hype, sensationalism or manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensational words that misrepresent scale (e.g., 'flood' vs small numbers). Visual actions that change reality may be fabrication. Consider different markets' thresholds; decisions to publish graphic material typically require senior-editor sign-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines and bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines should reflect presence at the dateline; datelines used only where staff/freelancers are on the spot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Byline stories only from places where the writer (or reporter being written up) was present. Include contributors in additional reporting lines with name and location. Datelines require staff or freelancers on the ground providing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly identify origin of material; avoid vague labels like 'handout' without source identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label material with specific source (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video', 'U.S. Army Photo'). Clearly attribute material not gathered by Reuters to allow audiences to assess reliability. Failure may be considered plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rumours
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to report facts, not rumours; exercise caution and verify; exceptional market-moving circumstances may be handled specially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate fact from rumour. When rumours move markets, attempt to track and verify or knock them down. In extreme market movement, a story may be moved before full verification following internal guidance (see The Essentials of Reuters sourcing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic images and obscenities
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish graphic or obscene material gratuitously; ensure valid news reason and usually senior-editor approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider necessity to understanding reality, potential distress, dignity of subjects and market thresholds. Senior editor decisions usually required; different distribution channels (broadcast clients vs consumer online) have varying acceptability. Mark stories ATTENTION EDITOR where required; consult Photos/Video sections and style guidance on obscenities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not allow personal or family investments to influence their work or use Reuters facilities for personal investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Reuters transaction/communication facilities for personal investment. Declare investments per Code of Conduct and adhere to higher standards in the Handbook's Personal investments section; disciplinary measures apply for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure no circumstances create a suspicion of bias from financial interests; declare and follow Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should read Code of Conduct and Personal investments guidance; changing regulatory environments require higher standards. Failure to adhere may lead to disciplinary action in the employee's location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work outside Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not undertake paid outside work without manager permission (writing, speaking, photography, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission will be granted routinely if activities do not conflict with Reuters. Guild members in US have some exceptions. Seek approval before book deals, paid talks, commercial photography, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking back with sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit stories to sources for vetting; limited verification is permitted but avoid giving sources chance to materially change quotes or facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist requests to approve quotes. You may check back to verify a quote or factual point, but avoid giving sources opportunity to retract or alter information to their advantage. If approval is sought, do not agree to material change; a tight deadline can be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept payments, gifts, services or benefits from news sources; accept nominal traditional gifts cautiously; surrender gifts of value to manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cultural sensitivity; nominal traditional gifts may be accepted, but gifts more than nominal value should be declined or surrendered for charity. Hospitality for newsworthy occasions may be acceptable within reason; do not accept 'junkets'. If in doubt, discuss with manager and follow Reuters bribery/corruption policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters staff should generally pay their own way; accept free travel/accommodation only with manager permission and usually only when necessary for access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where impractical to pay, consult manager; permission normally given only if story warrants coverage. Consider donations to charity equivalent to costs if accepting sponsor travel. Exceptional cases (war zone flights, military transport) require manager approval and weighing of conflict-of-interest risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bribes and other inducements
rubrics_metrics.description: Never take or offer payments for stories; entertain sources within reasonable bounds and per bribery policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering or accepting payments is a grave breach. Entertainment should be modest and news-driven. Be aware of local legal restrictions on gifts to government officials. Limited narrow exceptions exist but require approval and accurate recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence Within Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain editorial independence from Reuters commercial interests; do not alter coverage to suit company sales or contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sound news judgment; if non-editorial colleagues challenge balance, evaluate complaint. Trust Principles and Board exist to protect independence; escalate concerns where commercial pressures appear to conflict with editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and receiving awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may submit work for reputable awards with manager approval; avoid entering awards from parties with self-serving aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek manager approval to submit work done for Reuters. Do not produce work primarily for award entry. Approvals granted for reputable professional bodies; not for companies or interest groups that could influence impartiality. Report unsolicited awards immediately to manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take no side, tell all sides
rubrics_metrics.description: As Reuters journalists, do not identify with any side; reflect all relevant sides in text and visual stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure stories consider multiple perspectives; balance need not be equal space if one side warrants less. Avoid biased language and ensure fairness by seeking comment from those affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion and Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep factual news separate from clearly labelled opinion pieces; analysis may provide insight but must not stray into opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists do not express personal opinions in news stories or work-related blogs. Opinion pieces must be clearly labelled and carry disclaimers. Analysis should be supported by facts and named sources; avoid ungrounded assertions in columns and opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminatory language and stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inappropriate references to gender, ethnicity, religion, culture, appearance, age, sexual orientation and national stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral, natural language; avoid gratuitous references to appearance. Use plural, gender-neutral professional group terms. Question relevance of identity details and their placement in the story. Consult 'Reporting about people' section for more guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not express personal views on investments; reports with value judgments must be sourced to named third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters reports news and does not give investment advice; local laws may prohibit it. Do not provide investment advice to readers or customers in any medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Take extreme care reporting on Reuters or its subsidiaries; special rules apply to avoid perceived bias or market-moving effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories about Reuters must be marked ATTENTION EDITOR and seen by a regional specialist editor or deputy before transmission. Seek comment from authorised company spokesman. No unnamed-source quotes about Reuters. Pick-ups about Reuters should be ATTENTION EDITOR and carefully considered for market impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and Community Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters does not support or take sides with political parties or groups; staff should avoid activity that compromises neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff must avoid political activity that could create perception of partisanship; consult manager and Code of Conduct for permitted outside activities. (Section truncated in this excerpt — escalate queries to manager.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle complaints promptly, escalate when needed, mirror medium of complaint and keep complainant informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and escalate complaints that involve legal issues, claims of bias or requests to withdraw content. Advise senior staff, follow up with complainant in same medium, keep notes/tapes of phone interactions, consult legal counsel for threats of legal action, and file editorial incident reports for serious matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention Editor items (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag high-risk or sensitive stories with ATTENTION EDITOR and accompanying explanation for senior/editorial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Err on the side of caution for taste, balance, fairness, legal risk or reputational harm. Send items to regional specialist editor or senior desk editor with explanation; consult legal counsel where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bankruptcy stories (ATTENTION EDITOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat bankruptcy/insolvency stories cautiously and mark ATTENTION EDITOR; be precise with legal terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comment from the company or indicate efforts to seek it. Use precise legal terms (bankruptcy, insolvency, liquidation) and be aware they differ by jurisdiction. Avoid over-colourful reporting that implies hopelessness and check facts carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil lawsuits (ATTENTION EDITOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report threats or filings of lawsuits only when sufficiently newsworthy and include comment from both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid running threats of lawsuit unless high-profile or market-moving; such stories should be ATTENTION EDITOR. If comment is unavailable but story must run, state efforts made to reach the party (e.g., 'did not respond to two voicemail messages').

rubrics_metrics.name: Contentious claims, allegations of wrongdoing and vituperative attacks (ATTENTION EDITOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow sources to make serious accusations from anonymity; allegations should carry comment from the accused and be ATTENTION EDITOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnamed sources may be used only for facts, not opinions or vituperation. If a source makes allegations, require on-the-record status unless exceptional senior-official policy statements. Always seek comment from the other party; such stories normally need ATTENTION EDITOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic details, obscenities and blasphemy (ATTENTION EDITOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic or obscene material should be run only with valid news reason and senior-editor sign-off; warn readers where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider distress, dignity and audience thresholds. Mark stories ATTENTION EDITOR with explanation and bracketed notices at top (e.g., 'Note strong language in paragraph 6'). Online desks must handle consumer-facing distribution appropriately and consult Style Guide entries on obscenities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legally dangerous material
rubrics_metrics.description: Be familiar with libel, defamation and privacy laws; file legally risky stories ATTENTION EDITOR and consult lawyers if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand country-specific laws and reporting restrictions. Senior editorial decision and legal consultation may be required before publishing material that poses legal risk to Reuters or staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories about Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories about Reuters, staff or operations must be ATTENTION EDITOR and cleared by senior editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stories should be written by senior journalists in the bureau and cleared by the regional specialist editor; seek comment from an authorised company spokesman and mark for review before transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and medical breakthroughs and sensational stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle sensational scientific/medical claims with utmost care, normally by a specialist or with specialist input; mark ATTENTION EDITOR when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require reputable named sources and expert verification. File ATTENTION EDITOR for major claims; avoid running sensational items (cloning, cures, life on Mars) without specialist assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any story that must be withdrawn should be filed ATTENTION EDITOR with an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reasons for withdrawal and escalate to senior editors for review and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hoaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify authenticity before using news; be suspicious of telephone, online or unsolicited claims and follow a checking drill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat unsolicited telephone information as suspect; ask for full name/title/number, verify via independent channels, telephone the person back, verify unsolicited electronic material, capture screenshots of online sources, delay if necessary until verification, and beware of April Fool hoaxes. Use the same skepticism for material picked up from other media.
